To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the fat content of human milk increases steeply as the milk is progressively emptied by the suckling infant and that this relationship explains changes in the average fat content consumed by the infant and within and between breastfeeds variability in the fatty acid composition of human milk.

the fat content of breast milk increases steeply as the infant empties the breast, that the fatty acid composition of breast milk is variable and that these changes may be important in determining the fat intake of breastfed infants.

the fat content of human milk changes as the breast is progressively emptied by the suckling infant and that these changes can explain differences in the fat content of breast milk between mothers and within individual mothers over 24 h.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the control of the synthesis and release of milk fat and its consumption by the infant.
the control of the fat content and fatty acid composition of human milk and the relationship between the composition of milk and its synthesis.
the relationship between milk fat content, the degree of breast empty, the rate of milk synthesis and the fatty acid composition of human milk.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the fat content of human milk is a function of the degree of emptying of the breast and the fatty acid composition is a function of both the degree of emptyin and the rate of milk synthesis.
the fat content of human milk is determined by the rate of milk synthesis and by the degree of breast empty.
the fat content of human milk is controlled by degree of breast emptiness.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the fat content of human milk increases with increasing degree of breast emptyness, but that the fatty acid composition of milk is relatively constant and is not influenced by the degree of breast emptyning.

the fat content of breast milk is determined by the degree to which the milk is emptied from the breast, and the fatty acid composition of milk fat is determined by the relative rates of synthesis of the different fatty acids in the human mamary gland.

the fat content of human milk increases steeply as the milk is expressed and the fat content of the milk consumed by an infant can be calculated from the fat content of a single milk sample and the rate of breast emptying of that breast.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the fat content of human milk varies with degree of breast emptyness.
it provides a simple, accurate and noninvasive method for the calculation of the average milk fat content of milk ingested by infants.
the degree of breast empty is a useful measure to predict the fat content of breast milk.
